---
title: "A high-probability school comparison withheld"
subtitle: "5.10 · the public twelve-school CDE example"
description: "Full-report cost of requiring the F-above-I direction under declared family restrictions."
---

Schools F and I share a grade in the three-grade optimum, although F above I has high posterior probability.
Requiring a specified direction and reoptimising the complete report measures its additional risk within the same
family. That difference includes the effects on all other stated and withheld comparisons. The tertiles and a
fixed-order four-grade comparison provide further reports that state the direction. Their results identify the
roles of the particular grouping and search restrictions without assigning an exclusive cause to the withheld pair.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **F above I** shows direction probability .9999. Of 175,099 three-grade reports that state it, the least-risk one has risk .064087, slightly above the overall optimum .063774.
- **I above F** reverses the required statement. The best report stating this direction has risk .112261; the posterior probability alone does not summarize its full-report cost.
- **The tertiles state it** uses the two tertile cuts. This fixed report states 48 pairs with risk .082255, so stating F above I does not require a fourth grade.
- **The higher-cost optimum** sets τ to .45. The optimum itself now states F above I and has risk .143197.

The table ranks the three best reports in the same three-grade family. The report stating F above I is second, while the next displayed report is third. The input check excludes self-comparisons.

The four-grade comparison keeps the posterior-mean order and changes the allowed family. Its risk is comparable under the same law, τ and weight, but its order-based optimum is not a global optimum over every four-grade report. The two compared families are not nested. Withholding can reflect several interacting restrictions; the page does not assign a single exclusive cause to every shared-grade pair.

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, as adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`). This deliberately spread twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools; prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated. CDE source conditions apply; the data are not relicensed, are provided as is without warranty, and imply no CDE endorsement.

The analysis concerns directional reporting of chronic absence within this subset. It neither computes Dashboard status-and-change colours nor establishes school quality, causal effects, statewide optimality or calibration. Shared grades do not imply equal absence probabilities.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

The following call extracts the F-above-I probability in the original case-study input order.

```r
library(postrank)
e <- postrank_pairwise(pr_case_cde$input)$e
1 - e[6, 9, 1]
```
:::
